create.name: JoAnna Hardy
create.bio:
JoAnna Hardy teaches insight meditation (vipassana) in the Theravada Buddhist tradition. Raised Catholic, she was drawn to quiet reflection from an early age, and after years of moving between several spiritual paths she settled in Buddhist practice. Today she leads silent retreats, including visiting retreats at the Insight Meditation Society, and teaches on the faculty of the University of Southern California, as a meditation trainer for Apple Fitness+ and with the Meditation Coalition, which she helped to found.

Much of her work joins meditation with ethics and social justice: she offers classes and workshops on how kindness, compassion and clear seeing meet questions of race, gender and exclusion, and she works with young people and private students. She is a co-author, with Matthew Brensilver and Oren Jay Sofer, of Teaching Mindfulness to Empower Adolescents, a handbook for educators. Her online course on metta for Lion's Roar walks beginners through loving-kindness practice step by step, and many of her talks and guided meditations can be heard on Dharma Seed, Ten Percent Happier and the Be Here Now Network.

books.title: Teaching Mindfulness to Empower Adolescents
books.author: Matthew Brensilver, Oren Jay Sofer, JoAnna Hardy
books.description: A practical guide for teachers and others who bring mindfulness to teenagers. It sets out principles and tools for inviting young people into an honest look at their own inner life, drawing on the adult's own practice.

courses.title: How to Cultivate a Loving Heart: The Buddhist Practice of Metta
courses.description: A self-paced online course with Lion's Roar in which JoAnna introduces loving-kindness meditation over ten short videos, five of them guided sittings. It comes with review notes and readings, including her own forgiveness practice.

free_resources.title: A Simple Forgiveness Practice
free_resources.description: A short written practice from JoAnna's website for working with forgiveness when loving feels hard. It can be downloaded and used on its own or alongside metta practice.
